pr_title: Bluetooth: Host: Fix bt_addr_from_str for str starting with ':'
pr_body:
The previous implementation would read from `addr->val[0]` before it was initialized if the input string started with a colon ':'.

Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/58504
pr_comments:
@alwa-nordic many of your issues have already been closed as duplicates. Should the duplicate be added here instead? 

@jhedberg It may be easier to follow what has been done vs what is a duplicate if you close the issues as "Closed as not planned" as that will make them appear with white rather than the purple "Fixed" color, so we can distinquish between what has been fixed and what is a duplicate or otherwise marked as something that shouldn't/ be/isn't fixed.

> @alwa-nordic many of your issues have already been closed as duplicates. Should the duplicate be added here instead?

I don't understand what the last part means. Does GitHub have something like "Fixes as duplicate: #xxxxx"?

EDIT: Looks like the GitHub documentation has something on this: https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/working-with-advanced-formatting/using-keywords-in-issues-and-pull-requests#marking-an-issue-or-pull-request-as-a-duplicate
I'll remove the 'Fixes:' for the duplicate issues.

> I don't understand what the last part means. Does GitHub have something like "Fixes as duplicate: #xxxxx"?

For Github issues, when you close them manually (like @jhedberg did), you can either click the standard "Close Issue" button: 
![image](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/2520413/64a13b6a-d709-48c9-ac98-4452ee7e16c9)

or you can expand the array and get "Close as not planned" which Github has defined to also encompass "duplicate"
![image](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/2520413/234d0924-ec5f-4ba7-8b1c-427f848b9c61)

When closing as "Close as not planned" the issue gets a different color indicating that nothing has been done to close the issue, which is the case for duplicates and false positives
I had a bug in my code `if (digit == 3)`. I added an extra test `test_reject_bad_colon` to catch this. I also applied the suggestions from @Thalley, and refactored away the need for `strlen_addr`.
I split the loop for readability. Now we verify the colons and parse the hex separately.

issue_context.title: [Coverity CID: 316114] Uninitialized scalar variable in subsys/bluetooth/shell/bt.c
issue_context.body:
Static code scan issues found in file:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/tree/dae79cefaabf63086946a48ccca4094f26f146c8/subsys/bluetooth/shell/bt.c

Function: `cmd_auto_conn`
Component: Bluetooth
CID: [316114](https://scan9.scan.coverity.com/reports.htm#v29726/p12996/mergedDefectId=316114)


Details:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/dae79cefaabf63086946a48ccca4094f26f146c8/subsys/bluetooth/shell/bt.c#L2522

Please fix or provide comments in coverity using the link:

https://scan9.scan.coverity.com/reports.htm#v29271/p12996.

For more information about the violation, check the [Coverity Reference](https://scan9.scan.coverity.com/doc/en/cov_checker_ref.html#static_checker_UNINIT). ([CWE-457](http://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/457.html))

Note: This issue was created automatically. Priority was set based on classification
of the file affected and the impact field in coverity. Assignees were set using the CODEOWNERS file.
comments: This is a valid minor bug. A read from uninitialized memory happens if invalid input starting with a ':' is provided to `bt_addr_from_str`. This is very minor. All access is in-bounds. The only effect is "garbage-in-garbage out". The correct behavior should be to return -EINVAL.

review_comments: Nice idea with the tests. Perhaps, since these test explicitly for `-EINVAL`, we should add that as the only return value in the documentation of `bt_addr_from_str`? i.e. `@retval -EINVAL ...`
